Subject: Re: postfix making too many queries to LDAP

Wietse Venema wrote:
> Rolf E. Sonneveld:
>   
>> with all due respect, I fail to see why we should stick to this 
>> dump-to-a-file technique, in this era of quad-core processors, gigabit 
>> backbones etc. Why can't we simply use LDAP queries, with smart caching 
>> of the results? What exactly is the bottleneck? Is this, because the 
>> OpenLDAP client routines don't cache?
>>     
>
> Caching does not help when some *sshole does a dictionary attack
> on your mail server. You can't cache all the non-existent names
> before the *sshole asks for them.
>
> In addition, each Postfix smtpd is a non-persistent processes.  To
> implement caching with non-persistent LDAP clients, they would have
> to store it in a shared local cache. Might just as well run a local
> LDAP replica.
>   

Maybe it helps to point out that even Microsoft does the same
with Exchange 2007. To operate an Edge Server (their naming
for the relay-only mailserver role) one installs a local
Active Directory instance (ADAM, Active Directory Application
Mode, 2003R2 feature) which gets filled with the subset of the
AD data that is neccessary for the mail lookups (this happens
non-continuously, too).

This might also be worth to consider with other mail systems.
MS provides an Active Directory to ADAM synchronizer, so one
can query agains a standalone Windows server (maybe even over
a dedicated network connection, if bandwidth is an issue)
instead of raising the load level on the global catalog servers.

-Chris
